description: Turn one product photo into a square Instagram Story ad image with room for a headline and price. Place that square on a tall 9:16 phone frame after download.
h1: Instagram Story Ad Images from a Square Product Photo
lead: Instagram Story ad images can start from one hot sauce bottle photo, with room for a headline and a price. You place that square on a tall frame after download.
steps_h2: How to Make a Square Story Image in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: The hot sauce goes into a square, and that square is what you drop onto the tall Story.

steps.d: Use the photo where the whole hot sauce bottle is visible, label included. That photo is what the Story frame is waiting for.
If someone should hold the hot sauce, pick a face and have them say the heat. Rewrite that sentence to match the Story price.
Take the square image, set it on a tall 9:16 Story frame, and add the price there. A spoken clip can go out with it.

faq.q: What is a Story ad template?
faq.a: A Story ad template is a square frame with room for the hot sauce and for a price you add later. The product stays fully visible, and you skip filming a new clip just to fill that frame. When you need a taller motion ad, start from [creator-style video ads](page:video-ads).

faq.q: How does a Story template become something I can post?
faq.a: You leave with a square you can place on the Story. Put the hot sauce photo in the frame, set the weekend price as the line you will read, and download.

faq.q: Why a template instead of filming a creator for Stories?
faq.a: Stories go stale when the offer changes and the creator is booked. Rewrite the price on this frame and post the new Story while that booking is still ahead.

faq.q: Who should build a Story from this frame?
faq.a: A shop that posts Stories every week, and the person who writes those posts. A hot sauce brand and the helper who handles its Instagram both need the product fully in frame.

faq.q: Can a beginner assemble a Story this way?
faq.a: Yes. Someone who has never opened a timeline can still do it. The three steps turn one sharp photo into a Story square, and you type the price on the Story after the square downloads.

faq.q: Which shops post this kind of Story?
faq.a: Shops that sell something a viewer should see in full. Hot sauce, a small pouch, and a folded scarf can each take this frame, with the price typed on the Story.

faq.q: Can the Story use the photo I already shoot for the shop?
faq.a: Yes. The hot sauce in the frame should be the hot sauce you ship, label and all. Your logo can sit in a corner the layout leaves open, and you do not need a new shoot for that.

faq.q: Which apps is the Story frame meant for?
faq.a: Instagram Stories is the home for this square. Set it on a tall 9:16 frame there. A Facebook Story can use the same square, and a feed post can keep it at 1:1. Use 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 only when the placement is no longer a Story.

faq.q: Do I need a paid subscription for Story templates?
faq.a: Yes. Starter is $24.50 a month with 200 credits, Pro is $35 with 300, and Premium is $63 with 600. Each photo is 24 credits. A video is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. You see the cost first. A failed run returns the credits. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: Can the Story run as a paid ad or as client work?
faq.a: Yes. Run it as a paid Story, leave it as an organic post, or send the square to a client who sells the same hot sauce.

faq.q: Why use a Story template instead of starting from scratch?
faq.a: Your time goes into the price and the heat, which are the words shoppers read. The hot sauce already has a place in the frame, so you can spend the edit on those words.

items.t: A Product Link Can Start It
items.d: Paste the product page. The item comes through, and this square stays the frame for the Story.
Choose an AI avatar to hold the product in the Story, and bring that person back next time.
Add a voiceover in the language your shoppers use, or a cloned voice the shop already records with. You can change any word before the Story goes up.
Describe the offer in a sentence. A script draft comes back, and you can rewrite it in the editor.
Shape the Story in the built-in editor, then download a file with no watermark.
Run the same photo for another setting or another language, in a batch if you have several offers, then publish to Instagram, Facebook, or TikTok. The API can start the next one from your catalog.
